values.value: How much customer data sits behind your sends — roughly how many contact properties are in use, and do you have custom objects as well as contacts and companies?
How much audience data there is, and how many pieces it is in

[{"value":1,"label":"Contacts and companies with mostly HubSpot-standard properties; a few dozen custom properties at most, and no custom objects."},{"value":2,"label":"A few hundred custom properties in use, deals or tickets read by marketing, and perhaps one or two custom objects."},{"value":3,"label":"Custom properties in the high hundreds or more, several custom objects with their own associations, and calculated or rollup properties feeding segmentation."}]
Settings then Properties gives you the count per object, and Data Model lists any custom objects.

migration-accelerator/capabilities/platforms/hubspot.yaml — object_catalog.crm_data_model, whose nouns these options are built from: contact_properties (with its custom, calculation and rollup subtypes), companies, deals, tickets, custom_objects ("Commonly reported ceiling is 10 custom object definitions with up to 1,000 properties each; treat the numbers as unverified" — which is why the top band says "high hundreds or more" rather than quoting a ceiling as fact) and associations. The base wording asked about "30-100 tables, moderate SQL", which describes Marketing Cloud's Data Extensions and Query Activities; HubSpot has neither, so the base question was unanswerable on this pair rather than merely awkward. Kept to SIZE ONLY — property counts and object types — so it does not restate slot 5, which asks whether the model is entangled with another team's system of record and whether it decomposes into a subscriber plus sendable tables. calculated_property_formula in the same manifest is why calculation and rollup properties are named at option 3: they are the ones that inflate the number AND the work.
